main.content:
==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|entraunce||obsolete}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{uder|en|frm|entrance||entry}}. Replaced native {{cog|enm|ingang||entrance, admission}}, from {{cog|ang|ingang||ingress, entry, entrance}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|ĕn'trəns|a=UK,US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɛn.tɹəns/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-entrance.wav|a=Southern England}}

====Noun====
{{wp}}
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} The action of [[entering]], or going in.
#: {{syn|en|ingress|entry}}
#: {{coi|en|make a grand '''entrance'''}}
#: {{ux|en|Her '''entrance''' attracted no attention whatsoever.}}
# The act of taking possession, as of property, or of office.
#: {{ux|en|the '''entrance''' of an heir upon his inheritance, or of a magistrate into office}}
# {{senseid|en|Q1137365}} {{lb|en|countable}} The place of entering, as a gate or doorway.
#: {{syn|en|entryway<id:Q1137365>}}
#: {{hypo|en|tradesman's entrance<id:entryway for service purposes>|arctic entryway#Noun|arctic entry#Noun}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=1|passage=‘It was called the wickedest street in London and the '''entrance''' was just here. I imagine the mouth of the road lay between this lamp standard and the second from the next down there.’}}
#: {{ux|en|Place your bag by the '''entrance''' so that you can find it easily.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The right to go in.
#: {{ux|en|You'll need a ticket to gain '''entrance''' to the museum.}}
#: {{ux|en|to give '''entrance''' to friends}}
# The entering upon; the beginning, or that with which the beginning is made; the commencement; initiation.
#: ''a difficult '''entrance''' into business''
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|I|iii|passage=Beware of '''entrance''' to a quarrel.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1794|author=Henry Hunter|title=Sacred Biography
|passage=in the entrance of the history of this great patriarch}}
# The causing to be entered upon a register, as a ship or goods, at a customhouse; an entering.
#: {{ux|en|His '''entrance''' of the arrival was made the same day.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} The angle which the bow of a vessel makes with the water at the water line.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1899| title=Practical Engineer - Volumes 19-20 |author=| page=197| passage=A coarse-lined ship, fig. 4, has an angle of '''entrance''' of about 40 deg., measured at the load-water line; while a fine-lined ship has only about half that angle.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} The [[bow]], or entire wedgelike forepart of a vessel, below the water line.
# {{lb|en|music}} The beginning of a musician's playing or singing; [[entry]].
# {{lb|en|Philippines}} {{ellipsis of|en||entrance fee}}.
#: {{ux|en|I want to go to this place but the '''entrance''' is too expensive.}}

====Pronunciation====

* {{IPA|en|/ɛnˈtɹæns/|a=UK,US}}
* {{rhymes|en|æns|ɑːns|s=2}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-entrance-verb.ogg|a=US}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[delight]] and fill with wonder.
#: {{ux|en|The children were immediately '''entranced''' by all the balloons.}}
#* '''1996''', {{w|Tab Murphy}}, {{w|Irene Mecchi}}, {{w|Bob Tzudiker}}, {{w|Noni White}}, and {{w|Jonathan Roberts (writer)|Jonathan Roberts}}, ''[[w:The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1996 film)|The Hunchback of Notre Dame]]'' (film)
